scope: Saved true full16 states; no runtime/config/threshold changes, no physical success claim
basis_note: Native rotated-triangle geometric XY basis, not OBJ texture UV and not an explicit strap-aligned yarn coordinate. Rotation matches v0.0.29 Dm2x2. u/v lengths and shear computed from actual saved triangle F.

topology.body_face_selection: explicit physical body-face labels mapped to imported rest mesh

limitations: Full geometry saved about 50 ms; every-step max-edge metrics locate threshold crossing but not edge identity between geometry frames.
Nearest distances are discrete cloth samples to exact bear triangles; they identify proximity, not contact force or continuous collision clearance.
Native per-material-pair forces are not available; causation remains an inference.
findings: The first violating edge is a front/held-handle grid diagonal, two stations beyond the grasp-center row toward positive material X, not a seam or body edge.
Both neighboring triangles have approximately unchanged native BW directional lengths but large material-axis shear; principal stretch and contraction describe bias deformation.
Native BW material axes are rotated-triangle geometric axes rather than an explicitly strap-aligned woven coordinate. OBJ texture UV does not define native shell material directions.

The violating edge is roughly 165 mm from the teddy, and all sampled front-handle points are at least 39 mm away. Local direct teddy pressure does not explain this edge deformation. Loading transmitted through the held handle is consistent with the observations; exact contact-force causation is not established.
Bag body and mouth maximum edge ratios are only 1.056 and 1.021 at failure. Making the entire bag wider is not directly targeted to the detected material failure.
The free back handle is near the teddy at 1.26 mm, so its draping/contact remains relevant to future insertion, although its maximum edge ratio is only 1.031 in this state.
verifiable_adjustments_without_relaxing_: First candidate: explicit local effective shear reinforcement on handle triangles, with body material and all original 1.15 strain/force/contact gates unchanged; rerun from true initialization and compare handle shear, principal stretch, raw forces, and ultimate release/settle. No specific coefficient is certified by this audit.

If modeling a doubled/reinforced effective strap, adjust its shear parameter explicitly. The current adapter overwrites mu with 50 N/m independent of thickness, so thickness/E changes alone do not directly address this shear mode and alter mass/contact geometry.
An alternative is a better justified strap-aligned material basis, if the native implementation supports it; that is a constitutive modeling change, not a numerical threshold change.

A lower-prestrain held-hand pose could also be investigated: current handle rotation raises this edge from 1.022 to 1.062 before teddy loading. Any pose change requires the original full robot/teddy clearance and grip checks again.
No claim that slowing alone will fix quasi-static shear under load; force traces and actual state comparisons would be needed.
